proposals.before: Dingguo wished to execute his minister Ying, magistrate of Feiru. The people of Ying and others reported Dingguo.
proposals.after: Dingguo wished to execute his minister Yingren, the magistrate of Feiru. Yingren and others reported Dingguo.
proposals.reason: 郢人 is the personal name Yingren (magistrate of Feiru), not “Ying” plus “people of Ying”; the second 郢人 repeats that same person.

proposals.before: Dingguo wished to execute his minister Ying, magistrate of Feiru. The people of Ying and others reported Dingguo.
proposals.after: Dingguo wished to execute his minister Yingren, the magistrate of Feiru. Yingren and others reported Dingguo.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 郢人 is a personal name throughout, not a place-based collective.

proposals.before: In the Yuanshuo era, the brothers of the man from Ying again submitted a memorial detailing Dingguo's crimes.
proposals.after: In the Yuanshuo era, Yingren's brothers again submitted a memorial detailing Dingguo's crimes.
proposals.reason: 郢人昆弟 means brothers of Yingren the magistrate, not “the man from Ying”.

proposals.before: In the Yuanshuo era, the brothers of the man from Ying again submitted a memorial detailing Dingguo's crimes.
proposals.after: In the Yuanshuo era, Yingren's brothers again submitted a memorial detailing Dingguo's crimes.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise misreads 郢人 as a place origin instead of the personal name.
English word order “Prince of Wu Bi” obscures that 濞 is the personal name Bi.

proposals.before: King Xiaoxiao of Liang was afraid and sent a general against them; they again defeated two Liang armies and the soldiers all ran back.
proposals.after: King Xiao of Liang was afraid and sent a general against them; they again defeated two Liang armies and the soldiers all ran back.
proposals.reason: Literal English doubles 孝 as “Xiaoxiao”; 梁孝王 is King Xiao of Liang.

proposals.before: Han bribed Eastern Yue; the Yue king betrayed Liu Bi. When he rode out to review the ranks, assassins ran him through, boxed his head, and relay riders galloped the news to the capital.
proposals.after: Han bribed Eastern Yue; Eastern Yue then deceived Liu Bi. When he rode out to review the ranks, assassins ran him through, boxed his head, and relay riders galloped the news to the capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 東越即紿吳王 attributes the deceit to Eastern Yue as a polity, not to a named “Yue king.”

proposals.before: Jinbei was spared because he had been held hostage.
proposals.after: Jibei was spared because he had been coerced.
proposals.reason: 濟北 is Jibei, not Jinbei; 劫 means coercion, matching the literal.

proposals.before: The King of Jinbei, on account of having been coerced, was not executed.
proposals.after: The King of Jibei, on account of having been coerced, was not executed.
proposals.reason: 濟北 should be romanized Jibei, not Jinbei.

proposals.before: Ban Gu’s verdict: Jing was enfeoffed while the dynasty was still raw—distant blood, yet a deliberate chess piece to anchor the Huai–Yangzi belt.
proposals.after: The appraisal says: Jing was enfeoffed while the dynasty was still raw—distant blood, yet a deliberate chess piece to anchor the Huai–Yangzi belt.
proposals.reason: Chinese only has 贊曰; “Ban Gu” is not in the source sentence.

decisions.reason: 肥如令郢人 names the magistrate Yingren; the second 郢人 is the same person reporting Dingguo, not a place-collective “people of Ying.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 肥如令郢人，郢人等告定國

decisions.reason: Literal English must likewise treat 郢人 as the personal name Yingren throughout, as confirmed by the singular silencing of 郢人 in the next sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臣肥如令郢人，郢人等告定國

decisions.reason: 郢人昆弟 means the brothers of Yingren, continuing the personal name from the preceding units, not “the man from Ying.”
The literal field repeats the same misreading of 郢人 as a place origin; Yingren’s brothers is the accurate rendering.
吳王濞 is title plus given name Bi; “Prince of Wu Bi” buries the personal name, while “Bi, Prince of Wu” makes the naming clear.
梁孝王 is King Xiao of Liang; “Xiaoxiao” wrongly doubles the posthumous name 孝.
東越即紿吳王 makes Eastern Yue the deceiving agent; inventing a “Yue king” and “betrayed” is not supported.

decisions.after: The King of Jibei was spared because he had been coerced.
decisions.reason: 濟北王 is the King of Jibei, not merely Jibei, and 以劫故 says he had been coerced rather than held hostage.
濟北王 must be romanized King of Jibei; Jinbei is a false reading of 濟北.

Although 贊曰 literally introduces an appraisal, identifying it as Ban Gu's verdict is a defensible authorial label in an idiomatic translation of the Hanshu and does not change the appraisal's substance.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted repair of 濟北 shows the English title value “Jinbei” was a mistranslation; the office/title remains 濟北王, correctly “King of Jibei.”
